watcherStopBoundaryFix.change: Decisive fix is the App openWorkspace main-actor hop guard: the closure drops a delivery whose watcher is no longer workspaceWatcher or is stopped (watcher === workspaceWatcher && !watcher.isStopped). WorkspaceEventWatcher also confines debounceTask, a stopped flag and a monotonic generation to its serial queue: the delivered-event path returns early when stopped, each debounce re-validates stopped/generation under the queue and invokes the handler inside that check, and stop() tears the stream down then applies flag/generation/cancel under the same queue (dispatch-specific marker keeps deinit and on-queue callers off queue.sync). start() re-arms under the queue, isStopped is public. The queue confinement closes the same shape at the source for races the App guard already made unreachable in practice.
watcherStopBoundaryFix.rootCause: A hosted fixture's own post.md write surfaced as an FSEvent ~310 ms after the write and its +300 ms debounce fired before makeHostedBatchWorkspace's workspaceWatcher?.stop() ran; the handler's already-queued Task { @MainActor } hop — which stop() cannot recall — landed behind stop(), delivering a handleExternalChange disk inspection between the Replace All press and its task's evaluation: refused(.externalObservationPending) before preparation began (CI #151; reproduced locally 5x in handoff 27b phases 1/1b; 27c #fileID/#line rework confirms the producer is the same chain — openWorkspace watcher closure -> refreshWorkspaceAfterFileSystemChange -> handleManagedWorkspaceSessionsExternalChange -> handleExternalChange at App/AppState+Workspace.swift:395 — with real FSEvents from fixture-setup writes observed hopping onto the main actor inside the pre-stop() setup window, ~29-42 ms before the press, authorization .allowed; hops landing after stop() are now dropped by the guard and startHeldBarReplaceAll waits out any in-flight pre-stop observation plus .allowed immediately before the click).

m3.finding: redo per review: all 28 Replace-row tests x10 under TEST_RUNNER_PLAINSONG_HOSTED_TRACE_STDOUT=1 = 280 executions, 0 failures, 150 passing checkpoint dumps captured. The only advancing=true producers observed near the press are (a) the test-injected refreshWorkspaceAfterFileSystemChange in the file-switch fixture — 10 dumps, PlainsongTests/EditorReplaceUIHostedLifecycleTests.swift:101, authorityGen=24 — and (b) real accepted watcher hops — 3 dumps, Plainsong/AppState+Workspace.swift:395 each immediately after 'watcherHop accepted' at :391, authorityGen=23, authorization=allowed, ~29-42 ms before the press (testHostedCollapseThroughTheDisclosureCancelsThePlanAndHidesTheRetainedValue 2x, testHostedCancelLeavingWhileFocusedHandsFocusToReplaceAllOrTheField 1x). An accepted hop proves isStopped==false at hop time, so those real FSEvents — fixture-setup filesystem activity (the fixture's own post.md/dir writes delivered across the sinceNow boundary through the watcher's ~300 ms FSEvents latency + 300 ms debounce) — hopped onto the main actor BEFORE makeHostedBatchWorkspace's workspaceWatcher?.stop(), inside the setup window between the row-owner mounts and the press; this is test-setup activity, not product self-trigger (nothing in product code writes under the watched fixture root during setup), and hops landing after stop() are dropped by the guard. On a slower CI runner the same delivery can still have its disk inspection pending at the press -> .externalObservationPending refusal — startHeldBarReplaceAll now waits for waitForHostedReplaceObservationQuiescence + authorization .allowed immediately before the click and asserts a replaceAllTask started. No spontaneous or unattributed producer appeared in 280 executions.
